questions.a: SUPERSESSION vs THE VOYAGE — press_office's charter says how_it_learns: 'By supersession, not in-place update.' That rule's why is about the DOCUMENT'S CONTENT: a superseded claim stays readable, so a piece is replaced rather than edited under itself (Law 7). This ticket's why is about CROSSINGS: which ones a node made and when. A journal of crossings does not edit content — it is what makes supersession legible, since 'superseded by' is an event with a date. They compose; no conflict.

THE ROAD IS NOT THE JUDGE — concept-piece's prove_gate is a human quorum signature and code-seam's is the tester; skills/sorted/SKILL.md warns explicitly not to collapse those hands. Registering a workflow path for concept-piece changes WHICH CROSSINGS EXIST, not who proves them. PROVEME for a concept-piece remains the signature gate described in press_office/proofs/PROOF.md.

A CONCEPT-PIECE NODE IS A DOCUMENT, AND ONE COMPONENT HOLDS MANY VOYAGES — read off disk, not assumed: concept-piece.json's members_so_far names a file path. press_office/ is the component; its three documents are three nodes. CLAUDE.md already settles the addressing ('a ticket's voyage freezes here when it proves out'), so three voyages in one history.json is the normal case, not an addressing problem to solve.

filed_edges: [CORPUS] BACKFILL OR START EMPTY? The two 2026-08-05 brief revisions (the node/leaf separation and the learning-block anatomy correction) already sailed. Either they become tickets and compile into history, or history starts at the build and those two live only in proofs/PROOF.md and git. Both are defensible and the answer depends on what the compile actually accepts — which is why this is named at BUILDME rather than decided at the cast. NOTE THE HAZARD: backfilled history is a record of truth written after the fact by the same hand that sailed it (Law 7).

[CORPUS] press_office HAS NO TICKETS AT ALL — this is the part that makes the node bigger than a schema edit. state.json is COMPILED from a component's tickets and never hand-edited, so 'give press_office a state' means there must first be tickets for it to compile. The second child exists for exactly this. A build that writes the two files directly is the hollow build tooth (ii) refuses.
